work_item.title: Dark/Light Theme Implementation
work_item.description: 🚩 AC Addressed (Required) Introduce light/dark theme selection entirely within the existing Python-rendered web UI. Ensure query syntax highlighting and result panels remain legible under both themes. Persist the user’s theme choice across requests using local storage. 💡 What do you want to accomplish? (Required) Improve user experience by allow users to toggle between dark/light themes. 📋 Testability Considerations (Required) Unit tests to check the new dark/light theme functionality.
acceptance_criteria: Users can toggle between dark and light themes via the UI.
Query syntax highlighting colors adjust correctly and remain legible in both themes.
Result panels display content clearly and legibly in both themes.
User's theme preference is saved in local storage and applied automatically on subsequent page loads.
Unit tests cover theme toggle functionality and persistence.

analysis.summary: Implement a toggle for dark and light themes in the existing Python-rendered web UI, ensuring syntax highlighting and result panels remain legible, with user preference persisted via local storage.
technical_requirements: Add light/dark theme toggle functionality within the existing Python-rendered web UI.
Ensure query syntax highlighting adapts and remains legible under both themes.
Ensure result panels are styled appropriately for both themes to maintain readability.
Persist the user's theme choice across requests using local storage.
Implement unit tests to verify dark/light theme functionality.

risks: Ensuring consistent and legible styling across all UI components under both themes.
Potential CSS conflicts or overrides in the existing styles.
Persisting theme preference reliably across different browsers and sessions.
Testing UI changes thoroughly without an existing theming framework.
analysis.recommended_approach: Introduce CSS variables or classes to define theme colors and styles. Modify the Python-rendered templates to include theme toggle controls and apply theme classes dynamically. Use JavaScript to handle toggle events and save the preference to local storage. On page load, read the stored preference and apply the corresponding theme. Write unit tests for the theme toggle logic and persistence.

implementation_steps.description: Add theme CSS variables and update presentation/styles.py to support light and dark themes

instructions: Define CSS variables for the light theme at the root level, e.g., --bg-color: #f8f9fa, --text-color: #333333, --primary-color: #0066cc, --syntax-keyword: #00008b, --syntax-string: #a31515, --result-bg: #ffffff, --result-text: #000000.

Define a .dark-theme CSS class that overrides these variables with dark theme colors, e.g., --bg-color: #1a1a1a, --text-color: #e0e0e0, --primary-color: #4da6ff, --syntax-keyword: #569cd6, --syntax-string: #d69d85, --result-bg: #2a2a2a, --result-text: #ffffff.

Modify existing CSS selectors for body, query syntax highlighting, and result panels to use these CSS variables instead of hardcoded colors. For example, body { background-color: var(--bg-color); color: var(--text-color); }, syntax highlighting classes use var(--syntax-keyword), var(--syntax-string), etc.
Ensure all UI components that display query syntax and results use these variables so they adapt automatically when the .dark-theme class is applied to the body.
Add CSS rules for the theme toggle button styling, e.g., .theme-toggle-btn with appropriate padding, border, cursor, and colors that adapt to the theme variables.

implementation_steps.validation: Verify that styles.py contains CSS variables for both themes, existing styles use these variables, and a .dark-theme class overrides them correctly.

implementation_steps.description: Add theme toggle button to the base HTML template and integrate JavaScript for toggle and persistence

instructions: Locate the main base HTML template rendering function or string in html_template.py where the header or navigation bar is defined.
Insert a button element with id='theme-toggle' and class='theme-toggle-btn' in the header area, with initial text '🌙 Dark Mode'.
Add a <script> block just before the closing </body> tag that implements the following logic:
- On page load, read the 'theme' value from localStorage.
- If the stored theme is 'dark', add the 'dark-theme' class to the <body> element and update the button text to '☀️ Light Mode'.
- Add a click event listener to the toggle button that toggles the 'dark-theme' class on <body>.
- On toggle, update localStorage with the current theme ('dark' or 'light').
- Update the button text accordingly ('🌙 Dark Mode' when light, '☀️ Light Mode' when dark).
Ensure the script is pure JavaScript and does not rely on external libraries.
Confirm the theme toggle button styling is consistent with the CSS variables defined in styles.py.

implementation_steps.validation: Confirm the base HTML template includes the toggle button and JavaScript that applies the theme class and persists the preference in localStorage.

implementation_steps.description: Add unit tests for theme toggle functionality and persistence

instructions: Create unit tests to verify the theme toggle JavaScript logic using a headless browser or DOM simulation framework if available.
Test that the toggle button exists in the rendered HTML from presentation/html_template.py.
Test that clicking the toggle button adds/removes the 'dark-theme' class on the body element.
Test that localStorage is updated correctly when toggling themes.
Test that on page load, the theme is applied based on the stored localStorage value.
If no JavaScript testing framework is available, create Python tests that render the HTML and verify the toggle button presence and script inclusion.
Add tests to presentation/styles.py if possible to verify CSS variables exist (optional).

implementation_steps.validation: Unit tests cover theme toggle button presence, toggle behavior, localStorage persistence, and initial theme application.

Added CSS variables for themes in styles.py, a toggle button and JavaScript in html_template.py to persist user preference in localStorage, and unit tests to verify toggle functionality and persistence.
